Context/Background: To find novel treatments and drug combinations that could effectively target colorectal cancer cells (CRCs) and lower the probability of disease relapse, we designed multiple different combinations between cisplatin, cannabidiol (CBD), and intermittent serum starvation (ISS) on colorectal cancer cell lines. We analyzed differentially expressed genes and affected pathways in colorectal cancer cell lines to understand further the potential molecular mechanisms behind the treatments and their interactions.
Prompt: Based on the results of the differential expression analysis of CBD vs DMSO in colorectal cancer cells, run a pathway overrepresentation analysis for statistically significant genes (up and down combined) against the Reactome database. Then, provide a discussion of any relevant affected pathways, highlighting important up and down regulated genes in each.  Focus on any mechanisms by which CBD may alter cancer related pathways.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
We analyzed RNA-seq differential expression (DE) results for cannabidiol (CBD) versus DMSO treatment in colorectal cancer (CRC) cell lines (dataset “ijms-24-14743-v2_crc_cells_cbd_vs_dmso_DEG.csv,” total rows = 20 130). Using an adjusted p-value cutoff of 0.05, 2 051 genes were identified as significantly changing (both up and down). We performed an over-representation analysis (ORA) of these 2 051 genes against the Reactome_Pathways_2024 library to uncover pathways potentially modulated by CBD.

Pathway Enrichments (Reactome ORA)  
Below are the top enriched Reactome terms ranked by adjusted p-value. All pathways include genes regulated (up and down combined) in response to CBD.

| Term                                                         | Overlap | Adjusted P-value  | Leading Genes (subset)                                  |
|--------------------------------------------------------------|---------|-------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
| Transcriptional Regulation by RUNX3                          | 29/86   | 1.02 × 10⁻⁶       | YAP1, NOTCH1, TCF7, FOXO3, SMAD3, CDKN2A, MDM2, KRAS, TP53 |
| Oncogene Induced Senescence                                  | 16/35   | 1.30 × 10⁻⁵       | RB1, CDKN2A, MDM2, MAPK1, TP53                          |
| TP53 Regulates Transcription of Cell Cycle Genes             | 19/49   | 1.33 × 10⁻⁵       | CDKN1B, PCNA, GADD45A, CCNB1, TFDP1, BAX, SFN, TP53     |
| Toll Like Receptor 3 (TLR3) Cascade                          | 31/106  | 9.03 × 10⁻⁶       | ATF2, RELA, MAPK1, JUN, CHUK, FOS, TP53                 |
| TRIF (TICAM1)-mediated TLR4 Signaling                        | 31/110  | 1.30 × 10⁻⁵       | ATF2, RELA, MAPK1, JUN, CHUK, FOS, TP53                 |
| Cytosolic tRNA Aminoacylation                                | 12/24   | 9.11 × 10⁻⁵       | AARS1, GARS1, SARS1, IARS1, TARS1, FARSB                |
| FOXO-mediated Transcription of Cell Cycle Genes              | 9/17    | 6.10 × 10⁻⁴       | SMAD2, CDKN1B, GADD45A, CAV1, FOXO3, KLF4               |
| Response of EIF2AK1 (HRI) to Heme Deficiency                 | 8/15    | 1.17 × 10⁻³       | PPP1R15A, DDIT3, ASNS, ATF3                             |
| Downregulation of TGF-beta Receptor Signaling                | 11/26   | 8.01 × 10⁻⁴       | SMAD2, SMAD3, SMURF2, TGFBR1, TGFBR2                    |
| Constitutive Signaling by AKT1 E17K in Cancer                | 11/26   | 8.01 × 10⁻⁴       | CDKN1B, MDM2, RICTOR, MTOR, FOXO3                       |
| Zinc Transporters                                            | 7/15    | 6.01 × 10⁻³       | SLC30A5, SLC39A6, SLC39A8                               |

Discussion  
CBD treatment in CRC cells significantly enriches pathways governing tumor-suppressive checkpoints, stress responses, and protein homeostasis:  
1. Cell-cycle/senescence control via p53/RUNX3 axes (e.g., CDKN2A, TP53, RB1, FOXO3) suggests CBD promotes tumor suppressor activity and growth arrest.  
2. Induction of oncogene-induced senescence and FOXO-mediated transcription of cyclin inhibitors (CDKN1B/p27) points to reinforced G1/G2 checkpoints.  
3. Modulation of TGF-β/SMAD signaling (SMAD2/3, TGFBR1/2) and RUNX3 transcriptional networks implicates anti-proliferative differentiation programs.  
4. Upregulation of stress pathways—EIF2AK1 (heme deficiency), Toll-like receptor cascades—indicates integrated endoplasmic reticulum and innate immune-like responses.  
5. Selective enrichment of aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases suggests translational reprogramming under CBD, potentially limiting proliferative capacity.  
6. Altered zinc transporter expression may interrupt metal-dependent enzymatic processes critical for DNA repair and redox balance.

Together, these findings support a model in which CBD reactivates tumor-suppressive programs (p53/RB), enforces cell-cycle checkpoints, and induces cellular stress/senescence, thereby attenuating CRC cell proliferation.

Key affected pathways and notable genes:  
– Cell-cycle arrest & senescence: CDKN2A (up), CDKN1B (up), TP53 (activation), RB1 (sensor)  
– Stress response: PPP1R15A, DDIT3, ATF3 (EIF2AK1 pathway)  
– TGF-β signaling: SMAD2/3, TGFBR1/2 (downregulation)  
– Immune/stress signaling: MAPK1, CHUK, RELA (TLR3/TRIF cascades)

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate directionality of key DE genes (CDKN1B, SMAD3, TP53) by qPCR or Western blot.  
2. Test functional senescence markers (SA-β-gal) and checkpoint activation (p21^CIP1) post-CBD.  
3. Investigate interplay between CBD-induced translational changes (aminoacylation) and proliferation.  
4. Examine whether CBD-mediated TLR3 signaling recruits immune-modulatory pathways in co-culture models.
